label: decaying trace of a recent letter a (1-3 steps back), input/delimiter phase
explanation: Fires in the original-input phase and on <DEL> on the 1-3 steps after the letter a was input. In the top examples activation peaks on the step two after an a and fades over the next few steps. It is strongest when a is at the start of the sequence (first_tok=a, repeated a a), where it reaches the max at step 2 or 3. It never fires at t=0 and is nearly silent in the copy phase (4% of mass, mostly recall_idx 0-1). Rate is 47% when prev_tok=a vs 5.5% overall. It is not token-selective for the current input. There is also a broad, weak background activation (lowest quartiles) at original-phase steps and <DEL> with no a in the sequence, which the predicate misses. A trace that is stale (a seen more than 3 steps ago, or late in long sequences) is often inactive, which costs precision for a plain seen(a) predicate (F1 0.60, mass 0.81). Dev: P 0.74, R 0.55, F1 0.63, mass recall 0.74.
